## ✨ Highlights

- 🔑 **A node's first boot prints no key any more - it shows a pairing code**: a new node makes its CA and its server certificate, nothing else - no admin certificate, no private key on the console, none left on its disk. A node that trusts nothing yet shows a one-time code, `pairing 9BC3-3016-3D39-2K7Q-M2XD`: the Controller's **Add node** or `janusctl fleet adopt -code` checks the node's certificate against it before sending anything, and gives it the fleet ([#465](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/465), [#466](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/466), [#469](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/469)).
- 🪂 **A warm standby for the Controller**: a second Controller copies the active every minute and takes over when you promote it - by hand, never by itself -, the same Controller one epoch above. The old active steps down when it sees its peer above it, or reads it in a **witness** - Consul's KV or the backups' S3 bucket - when it can't reach it ([#470](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/470), [#471](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/471)).
- 🛟 **Taking a node back without its fleet**: a `JANUSRESCUE` volume attached to a node opens its pairing window for 30 minutes, whatever it trusts: `janusctl access rescue` gets an hour's admin certificate of the node's own CA with the code from its console ([#468](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/468)). And with the Controller down, `janusctl login -kit` signs you an hour's certificate with the fleet's recovery kit ([#463](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/463)).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Add new nodes with this release's Controller or janusctl.** A node installed from this release has no `admin.crt` on its disk and no key on its console: a Controller or a janusctl from before this release has no way to add it (no pairing code). Nodes installed before keep their admin credential and are added as before (`.pfx` or PEM on **Add node**, `fleet adopt -ca -cert -key`).
- **janusctl's `-cert` and `-key` have no default any more** (they pointed at the node's `admin.crt`, which new nodes don't have): use a context (`janusctl login`, `janusctl fleet`) or give both. `janusctl access rotate-ca` loses `-console`: the node never prints a key.
- **`LocalCARotate` needs `admin_public_key`** - the node makes no admin key itself any more.
- **One Controller at a time on a data directory**: a second `dashboardd` on the same directory - a second container on the same volume, a `dashboardd restore` while it runs - stops at once and says which process holds it ([#462](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/462)).

## ⚙️ Node

- **The pairing window** ([#465](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/465), [the pairing code](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/internals/trust.md)):
  - A node that trusts no fleet and has no Controller provisioned opens a separate TLS listener on port **9506** (`-pairing-addr`), never the API's port: its certificate is made for the window, it asks no client certificate and serves one call, which gives the node a fleet. Port 9505 stays mutual TLS.
  - The code is 20 symbols: the first bits of the window certificate's SHA-256 (the client checks them before sending anything), a 36-bit secret (5 wrong ones close the window until the node restarts), and a check symbol that catches a typo before it costs a try.
  - New at each start, in memory only, good once; shown in the banner and on the console - never in janusd's log, LOGS or log forwarding. Every call is audited; a pairing publishes `access.paired`.
  - A node from before the code - its admin credential printed by its first boot - opens no window.
- **No admin credential at the first boot** ([#469](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/469)): the node logs `pki: first boot - generated a new CA in DIR`; the banner loses its orange "First boot" line. `pki: this node's CA: SHA-256 ...` is unchanged.
- **The rescue volume** ([#468](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/468), [when the Controller is down or lost](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/recovery.md)): `janusctl image rescue-volume [-fat] [-skip-firewall] OUT` writes it (an ISO for a CD-ROM, FAT for a disk or a USB stick). At every boot init looks for it; janusd then opens the pairing window for 30 minutes, its code shown as "rescue" on the console. `-skip-firewall` leaves the saved ruleset out that boot. The certificate (`rescue:<name>`, `os:admin`, an hour) is audited and publishes `access.rescue_issued`.
- **A firewall ruleset confirmed just before a power cut is kept** ([#467](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/467)): the rename of the saved ruleset waited for ext4's next journal commit - a node powered off within 5 seconds of a confirm booted unfiltered. The saved VRRP, BGP and Consul configurations had the same gap.
- **The node page's LOGS tile says how far back the logs go** ([#460](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/460)): the span the ring holds ("2d 9h"), its fill around it, since when, its boots and the rate it's written at - a full ring is its normal state, not a warning.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Add node by its pairing code** ([#466](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/466)): the form defaults to the code (and the pairing address, the API's host on 9506 unless told); the fleet must be set up first. The node trusts the fleet at once, and the Controller keeps no credential. An older node's `.pfx` or PEM stay as the other two choices.
- **The warm standby** ([#470](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/470), [a warm standby for the Controller](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/controller-standby.md)):
  - **Settings › High availability › Add a standby** gives a pairing token, good once for an hour; `dashboardd standby -peer ACTIVE:8443 -pair TOKEN` pairs a new data directory with it. The standby runs none of the Controller's loops: it copies the active's data directory and master key every minute (not the nodes' configurations) over the registration port, each pinning the other's certificate.
  - `dashboardd promote` on the standby's host, or **Switch over** on the active's card, makes it the active: the active hands a last copy over when it answers; otherwise the last copy, at most a minute old - refused while the active answered less than 2 minutes ago, unless `-force`.
  - The epoch fences the old active: a Controller that finds its peer active above its epoch becomes its standby - at its start, before any loop, and every 30 s -, what it held set aside in `<data>/ha/previous/`.
  - `GET /api/ha/active` answers 200 on the active only, for a keepalived `track_script` in front of both. `dashboardd ha status` says where a data directory stands.
- **The witness** ([#471](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/471), [the witness](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/controller-standby.md#the-witness)): a record both Controllers reach when they can't reach each other, signed by the HA key of the one holding the epoch - in **Consul's KV** when Settings › Consul is on (the Controller's token needs `key_prefix "janus/controllers/" { policy = "write" }`), else in the **backups' S3 bucket**. A promotion writes its new epoch there first - refused, unless forced, when it can't - and the active reads it every 30 s: cut off from its standby, it steps down within 30 s of a promotion. Writes are check-and-set (Consul) or conditional (S3 `If-Match`/`If-None-Match`). The High availability card shows where it is, its epoch and whose.
- **A backup restored on another host follows it** ([#463](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/463)): the identity is renewed for the new host's addresses (the old ones kept), nodes using the Let's Encrypt relay are given its new URL, and the first start logs what still names the old host.

## 💻 janusctl

- `janusctl fleet adopt NAME -endpoint ADDR -code CODE` ([#465](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/465)): pairs a node that trusts nothing yet into a fleet without a Controller.
- `janusctl login -kit KIT [-role ROLE]` ([#463](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/463)): with the Controller down, an hour's certificate for the context's key, signed with the fleet's root from the recovery kit (`kit:<account>` in the nodes' logs). Nothing changes on the nodes; once the Controller is back, `janusctl login` as before.
- `janusctl image rescue-volume` and `janusctl access rescue` ([#468](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/468)).

## 🧩 Clusters

- **An update in place can wait for the balancer and hand connections over** ([#461](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/461)) - the Update dialog, `POST /api/clusters/{id}/upgrade`, `janusctl cluster upgrade`, each choice greyed out with why when the cluster can't have it:
  - **Wait for the balancer**: before a member goes, every other is in service by the balancer hook (RouterOS, or a webhook's new `check` event); a member goes out once drained and comes back once undrained, two minutes each; a pause between members (`settle_seconds`).
  - **Hand the open connections over** (anycast clusters with nftables): the member going out refuses new connections, the others copy the packets of its open ones to it (`nft dup`) until they end or the grace runs out; back, it holds - drops, not resets - the packets of connections it has no trace of while the others' readings catch up. The kernels get `NFT_DUP_IPV4`/`NFT_DUP_IPV6`.
